claims.claim: Removed VP03 issuer, broker, provenance-owner and handoff dependencies from the six production integrations. Retired all six listed VP03 modules, six focused tests and six versioned documents; no remaining source, test or package-entrypoint references demand those modules.

Public terminal transport uses a bounded deterministic projection within review_transport. It preserves canonical identities, source commands and verification metadata while replacing workspace/raw locators and diagnostic text, retaining private original files locally.

Runtime completion retains admitted TASK/RUN/candidate binding, Runtime-owned verification and canonical evidence construction, executor-proof rejection and existing single-terminal handling without provenance issuance or checkpoint authority.

AUTHOR_TASK, SUBMIT_REVIEW, AUTHOR_REPAIR and AUTHOR_REMEDIATION retain existing identity, expected-main/CAS and correction lineage checks. Git writers use the existing subprocess credential path without broker routing or privilege fallback.

Publisher and recovery retain reviewed-source binding, shared reservation, currentness, CAS and replay/conflict checks. Privacy comparisons preserve lifecycle bindings across private and public views without an issuer or broker dependency.

The forward commit leaves canonical artifacts, historical refs, minimum-sufficient-v2 policy and Frozen Kernel/KA01 documents unchanged. Legacy decoding and terminal replay paths remain, with no TASK-333 replay, TASK-334 alteration, new scheduler or intra-PRIMARY correction capability.

Added regression cases for public RESULT/FAILURE serialization, source conflicts, legacy replay, retired broker configuration, PRIMARY proof rejection and V2 metadata preservation. Existing admission, correction, reviewer ingress, publication/CAS, recovery and workflow compatibility cases remain.
The committed candidate changes only 28 files from the exact permitted modification list, and the worktree is clean.
